source.title: Exploiting Explainable Metrics for Augmented SGD
source.authors: M. S. Hosseini; Mathieu Tuli; K. Plataniotis

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper, including appendices; some table values appear flattened, with means and standard deviations run together.
record.tranche_reason: Compares optimizers on held-out performance and measures correlations between newly proposed weight metrics and generalization gap. These are conceptual tests of optimizer-related generalization and network properties, not the claim versions’ exact interventions or measures.
record.gate_note: The paper reports optimizer comparisons and correlations for its stable-rank, condition-number, and quality metrics. Figure 4 includes batch-size comparisons, but the supplied text gives no batch-size-specific values or explicit comparison against smaller batches under a fixed epoch budget. Cited findings about other work are not recorded as results.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares Adam and momentum SGD on held-out image-classification performance under learning-rate tuning with other optimizer parameters largely fixed. These results test V4. Its low-rank metrics do not measure V7's magnitude-aware sharpness.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors present stable rank, condition number, and their combined quality measure as indicators of learning and generalization, and argue that using stable-rank changes to adapt per-layer learning rates yields competitive or improved performance with low computational overhead. They acknowledge competitive alternatives and similar optimizer performance on MHIST.
record.recipe_differences: The optimizer comparisons use the paper's own RMSGD procedure and optimizer configurations; the network-property measure is a new quality metric, not magnitude-aware sharpness.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors state that performance depends on optimizer, dataset, network, batch size, and learning-momentum setting; the supplied text gives no explicit batch-size-specific results.

fits_no_version.finding: The low-rank quality measure correlates with generalization gap and test accuracy across optimizer and network configurations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A quality measure derived from low-rank weight spectra can indicate held-out performance and generalization gaps.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors describe RMSGD as robust across batch sizes and state that scaling batch size can degrade SAM's performance; the supplied text does not establish the budget-controlled comparison required by V5.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Batch-size sensitivity depends on the optimizer, with per-layer learning-rate adaptation potentially improving robustness.

record.problems: The generalization metric correlations are largely presented in figures and aggregate coefficients; the supplied flattened tables complicate precise interpretation of some means and standard deviations. The optimizer accuracy comparisons do not establish whether Adam had equal or better training performance.
record.rows_left_out: No additional optimizer accuracy rows were extracted beyond the ResNet18 Adam-versus-SGD comparisons on CIFAR10 and CIFAR100. Other optimizer comparisons are reported in Tables 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, and 8, but the catalog version's specific Adam-versus-SGD comparison is represented by these two datasets. Metric-correlation results do not measure V7's magnitude-aware sharpness and are recorded under fits_no_version.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, chance-level random-label test accuracy, and coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Width sweeps beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity.

Readable results establishing equal or better Adam training performance; broader hyperparameter tuning; switching from Adam to SGD; and recovery through decoupled weight decay. Language-model configurations are described, but no language-model outcomes are supplied.

A batch-size comparison with an identifiable fixed epoch budget and readable outcomes. The prose reports batch-size sensitivity, but does not establish this version's budget-controlled large-batch penalty or its removal.
Dropout interventions, small-data dependence, excessive-dropout underfitting, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-scaled weight-perturbation sharpness and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures among networks with similarly low training loss.
Removing highly memorized training examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: The supplied text contains additional V4 comparisons explicitly declared in rows_left_out, so they are not listed as missing. They warrant separate condition-specific rows before further verdicts: for example, on MHIST ResNet34, Adam accuracy is 81.02 versus SGD's 79.65, and Adam AUC is 87.90 versus 86.57. The authors describe MHIST optimizer performance as similar overall. The R1–R2 support verdict therefore applies only to their CIFAR conditions. Figure captions mention training curves, but their values are unavailable in the supplied text. The study is not an original source for any listed version.

Dropout effects and removing dropout or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the effect on test accuracy.

relationships.display_finding: The reported lower Adam test accuracies than momentum SGD on both datasets remain unverified, without established matching training performance.
